title: A linearly stable excited dark-matter core, proved across its window up to 0.002-wide edge brackets: certified spectral stability of the one-node Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson state for every central amplitude in [1597/1000, 1983/1000], and certified brackets of its stability-band edges
description:
In plain words. If dark matter is an ultralight particle, it can settle into a ball held together by its own gravity. The next ball up from the simplest one has a hollow shell inside it, and such balls are usually unstable. A 2024 numerical study (arXiv:2402.07998) found a narrow window of central densities in which the one-shell ball survives every small shake. Version 1.0 of this work proved linear (spectral) stability, with computer-checked error bars, at nine points of the window, and certified where the window ends. Version 2.0 proves it for every central amplitude from 1.597 to 1.983: one core for each amplitude, forming one continuous family of one-shell cores, each spectrally stable. With the certified unstable points 1.595 and 1.985, the stable window is pinned to within 0.002 at each end.

Result C (version 2.0; proved, computer-assisted with interval arithmetic; internally AI-refereed; not checked in a proof assistant). For every sigma0 in [1597/1000, 1983/1000] there is a decaying one-node solution of the repulsive Gross-Pitaevskii-Poisson system with sigma(0) = sigma0, continuous in sigma0, equal to the certified state at 23 rational nodes and unique in an explicit ball around a cubic Hermite predictor; for each of these states the linearised operator J L on L^2(R^3) has no spectrum with Re lambda > 0. The proof certifies a drop in the inertia of L + i w J between two frequencies (the classical local Krein index identity of Kollar-Bosak and Kollar-Miller, used here as a computer-assisted certificate), makes it uniform on each of 22 cells by a convexity cover with closed-form chord bounds decided as exact quadratic tests, and encloses the family of states between nodes by a Newton-Kantorovich argument whose residual vanishes like t^2(1-t)^2 at the nodes. Sealed test BAR-W1: 22 of 22 cells, 23 of 23 nodes and 16 of 16 controls HOLD; tightest margin ratio 2.336. An independent exact-rational checker found 0 problems. One control rule (XU at 1985/1000) was set after seeing that control's data, before the seal; it concerns frequencies near the counter's upper limit (w ≈ 2.59), far above those the proof uses, and is disclosed.

Result A (version 1.0, computer-assisted). At sigma0 = 9/5 exactly, J L has no spectrum with Re lambda > 0; its spectrum lies on the imaginary axis. The proof certifies the state (E = [-3.10544025447 +/- 3.02e-12]), brackets the Morse indices of L+ (with its nonlocal Poisson term) and L- in every angular sector (n(L+) = (2, 1, 1, 0), n(L-) = (1, 1, 1, 0) for L = 0..3, none beyond), certifies a negative-Krein imaginary eigenvalue at L = 0, 1, 2, and closes with a direct Hamiltonian index inequality. A blind float replication from the paper alone reproduced every count and all six Krein frequencies to ten digits (sealed pass rule: relative 1e-4; the ten-digit agreement is a POST HOC observation).

Result B (version 1.0; float map, certified grid and edge brackets). The common stability band is [1.5963117, 1.9841288] (float), narrower than the published 1.55-2.07. Both edges are Krein collisions (float): L = 0 below, L = 2 above (sectors as in Fig. 8 of arXiv:2402.07998). A sealed certified test proves linear stability at nine points and linear instability (a certified growing quartet) at 1595/1000 and 31/20 (L = 0) and at 2 and 1985/1000 (L = 2), so the edges lie in certified brackets [1.595, 1.597] and [1.983, 1.985].

Not claimed. Nonlinear or orbital stability; uniqueness of the state beyond the stated ball; the exact edge points; any statement about real halos. To our knowledge (search of arXiv, INSPIRE and Zenodo to November 2026), no earlier computer-assisted proof of spectral stability on a whole parameter interval exists for a Hamiltonian state with Krein-signed spectrum and a nonlocal kernel; the local Krein index identity is classical, and interval-wide stability proofs exist for other equations (Barker 2014; Breden, Payan, Reisch and Tang 2025; Braz e Silva 2026), credited for method.

Checks. Sealed tests, all listed (one duplicate seal VOID); internal hostile referee rounds and engine audits (internal lab checks, not external peer review); a blind replication of the 9/5 result; an independent exact-rational checker of every window output with mutation tests; a number checker that ties every printed number to its file.

Prepared with AI assistance; what was checked, and by what, is stated above.
